clue.text: What over-eating distends by about 45 inches

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word by is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
an ell is an old measure of cloth, 45 inches long

explanation.surface: A glutton's waistline swells by nearly four feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ELL, the old 45-inch cloth measure, inside BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating swells the stomach, the abdomen that bulges after a big meal.

clue.text: Storey reconstructed for a pearl supplier

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building floor is rebuilt for a jewellery dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructed' rearranges the letters of STOREY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearls grow inside this shellfish, so it supplies them.

clue.text: Why the chimney smokes when there is gas in mine

explanation.surface: A chimney belches smoke when a mine fills with gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the first part explains a smoky hearth: the fire is damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blaze smokes; separately, methane in coal pits is the miners' explosive hazard of that name.

clue.text: Take heart when Guevara turns pure

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: turns tells us the word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Feel encouraged when the revolutionary becomes virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reads PURE backwards as ERUP, placed after CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is to become more hopeful, the same as brightening in spirits.

clue.text: Hair style for a school's annual turn-out

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a crop is a farm's yearly yield

explanation.surface: A haircut chosen for a school's yearly parade.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the English boarding school; 'turn-out' here is the year's harvest, not a parade. An Eton crop is a short, slicked 1920s women's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a fashionable short bob worn by women in the 1920s.

clue.text: Sort of eggs best for cooking on a priceless stove

parts.note: costing nothing, so free
a range is a large kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: The best eggs are cooked on an antique, invaluable stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priceless' suggests precious, but here means costing nothing. A range is a big kitchen cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs labelled this way come from hens allowed to roam outdoors.

clue.text: Pistol which adds little weight to a night-fighter's kit

definitions.text: adds little weight to a night-fighter's kit

explanation.surface: A gun that is barely felt in a night soldier's pack.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very pistol fires flares, named after Edward Very; read as ordinary words, the item weighs very little.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very flare is fired from a signal gun; and something barely heavy adds hardly any weight.

clue.text: A sound stalk is needed for a baby carrier

indicators.note: a sound of a word means how it is pronounced, so we want a word said like the next one

parts.note: a plant stem

explanation.surface: A healthy stem is required for something that carries an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but signals a homophone: in British speech the two words are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore says this bird delivers newborns to parents.

clue.text: Part of Saddam's cudgel

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A piece of the Iraqi dictator's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to letters inside saddam'S CUDgel; whole, the clue describes a missile from Saddam Hussein's armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Scud missiles were the ballistic weapons Iraq fired in the Gulf War, part of its weaponry.

clue.text: No one is either absent or absent minded

explanation.surface: Nobody is missing, and nobody is daydreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a full attendance, and also mentally sharp; 'not' this phrase would be absent-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A full register means everyone is present; and someone mentally alert is never vague or forgetful.

clue.text: Henry's second wife entered Civil Service film festival

indicators.note: entered means went into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Anne Boleyn was Henry VIII's second wife

explanation.surface: A Tudor queen joins the civil service for a movie event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts ANNE (Boleyn) inside CS.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera town hosts the world-famous annual cinema event, so it stands for the festival.

clue.text: Publicity man taking a boat from Malaya which is.

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

explanation.surface: A spin doctor acquires a Malayan vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'which is.' runs into the next clue and plays no part here.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay sailing canoe with an outrigger.

clue.text: … going-by the lower route

explanation.surface: Travelling along the bottom path.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 'which is' from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A project in motion is progressing; and the path beneath is literally the under way.

clue.text: Plough providing thrills at the amusement park

definitions.text: providing thrills at the amusement park

explanation.surface: Farm work turned into a funfair ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough is the British name for the star group Americans call by this name; in Britain it is also a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven-star constellation pattern goes by both names; and a fairground roller coaster carries this name in Britain.

clue.text: How to keep a briar polished in the Arabian desert

definitions.text: How to keep a briar polished in the Arabian desert

parts.words: How to keep a briar polished in the Arabian desert
parts.note: a briar is a tobacco pipe, rubbed with lubricant to shine it; in Arabia the same two words describe a pipeline carrying petroleum

explanation.surface: Caring for a smoker's pipe in Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing grease on a smoking pipe keeps it shiny; across Arabia petroleum flows through such conduits.

clue.text: Unbeatable, government would be if the Upper House were abolished

definitions.text: government would be if the Upper House were abolished

explanation.surface: An invincible government, imagined without the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The Upper House is the House of Lords, filled with peers; without it, parliament has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal cannot be bettered; and without the Lords, lawmakers would lack nobles.

clue.text: Percolation must be dealt with elsewhere in the book

definitions.text: must be dealt with elsewhere in the book

explanation.surface: Leakage is a topic covered in another chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is a cross-reference instruction in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly oozing through soil is percolation; and 'go to another leaf' is a cross-reference note.

clue.text: Neanderthaler who rose with the lark

explanation.surface: A caveman who got up at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Prehistoric humans are called this; taken literally, a person up at dawn is an early riser.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthals were prehistoric humans; and a dawn riser is someone up before others.

clue.text: Highly trained Pole ended life

parts.note: S is the South Pole
to kill is to end a life

explanation.surface: A trained Polish person died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests someone from Poland, but here is the South Pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expert has been thoroughly taught and practised.

clue.text: Lazy speech leads to gossip

explanation.surface: Careless talk leads to rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy speech is literally talk of the indolent kind; and gossip is chatter without purpose.

clue.text: A capital orchestra too!

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, London being the capital

explanation.surface: A London orchestra, as well!
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' refers to London, giving the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: Genuine eighth of a piece of eight

definitions.text: eighth of a piece of eight

explanation.surface: An authentic fraction of a pirate's coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A piece of eight was a Spanish dollar worth eight of these silver coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine means authentic; and the old Spanish silver coin was one eighth of a dollar.

clue.text: Wealth in the form of collections

explanation.surface: Riches held as collected items.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer means forming groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Resources and property make up wealth; and grouped items form sets.

clue.text: A party on the navy deck

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A celebration held on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's floor but is the verb meaning decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate or embellish.

clue.text: Fruit which must be very soft if put in alcoholic beverages

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ales are beers
pp is pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Fruit gets mushy when soaked in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places PP, the music marking pianissimo, inside ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: These orchard crops are a common kind of fruit.

clue.text: Put down a team as reserve

parts.note: to lay is to put down
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team is dropped to the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a noun, a substitute player, but is the verb to keep back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to save it for later use.

clue.text: Be a pious man? Anything but!

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: Be a saint? Far from it!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads off the wordplay: a brute is the opposite of a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is the very opposite of a saint.

clue.text: Stage-smitten woman of ill-repute to begin new work

indicators.note: smitten means struck, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a tart is slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A theatre-struck loose woman starts a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smitten' rearranges STAGE as GETAS, followed by TART.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to commence, as in getting going on a new job.
